## Before submitting

- [x] I agree to license this contribution under the terms of [LICENSE.txt](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/LICENSE.txt).
- [x] I ran `pre-commit run` and committed any formatting changes.
- [x] I reviewed the Hard Rules in the `AGENTS.md` for each directory this PR touches (see [root AGENTS.md § Reviewing a PR](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/AGENTS.md#reviewing-a-pr-human-or-agent)) and my changes comply, or I explain the exception below.
- [ ] I added GitHub labels: one `cat-*`, one or more `area:*` / `op:*`, and one `orig-*` (see [label list](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/labels)).

## Affected area

FE OSS kernels or CuTeDSL

- `python/cudnn/gemm/frost/sm120/kernel_templates/sm120_moe_grouped_matmul_fwd.py`
- `python/cudnn/gemm/frost/sm120/kernel_templates/sm120_moe_grouped_matmul_fwd_swap_ab.py`
- `python/cudnn/gemm/frost/sm120/kernel_templates/sm120_moe_grouped_block_scale_matmul_fwd.py`
- `python/cudnn/gemm/frost/sm120/kernel_templates/sm120_moe_grouped_block_scale_matmul_fwd_swap_ab.py`
- tests: `test/python/gemm/frost/gemm_test_utils.py`, `test_moe_grouped_matmul_fwd.py`, `test_moe_grouped_block_scale_matmul_fwd.py`

## Summary

The grouped persistent scheduler of the four SM120 MoE templates now converts its warp ballot to `Uint32` before the bit reverse and bit find that pick the winning lane:

```python
winning_lane = cutlass.Int32(31) - cute.arch.bfind(cute.arch.brev(cutlass.Uint32(thread_succeed))).to(cutlass.Int32)
```

`cute.arch.bfind` then emits `bfind.u32` instead of `bfind.s32`. For each of the four kernels (bf16 and NVFP4, both orientations), the PTX differs from develop in this one instruction only.

Two tests (four cases) are added. `gemm_test_utils.py` gains `keep_kernel_ptx` / `kernel_ptx`, which compile a plan with `--keep-ptx` (persistent compiled cache off; PTX files and generated sources under the test's tmp dir) and read the PTX back, and `brev_bfind_types`, which lists the type of every `bfind` that reads a `brev.b32` result in the same PTX function.

## Why

The scheduler warp finds the group that holds a claimed tile with a ballot over 32 consecutive groups. The groups' prefix ends never decrease, so the ballot is a suffix mask and the winner is its lowest set lane, computed as `31 - bfind(brev(ballot))`. The ballot is an `Int32` (`nvvm.vote_sync(..., BALLOT)`), `brev` keeps the type, and `cute.arch.bfind` emits `bfind.s32` for an `Int32` operand. `bfind.s32` returns the position of the highest bit that differs from the sign bit. When every lane succeeds (lane 0 wins: ballot `0xFFFFFFFF`, `brev` gives -1) it returns `0xFFFFFFFF`, and `winning_lane` is `31 - (-1) = 32`.

Lane 0 wins on most launches: the CTA that claims tile 0 takes this path whenever group 0 has rows, and so does a claim that falls in the first group of a later 32-group window. Any other claim that finds its group is won by a higher lane; bit 0 of the ballot is then clear, `brev(ballot)` is non-negative, and `bfind.s32` already returned the right lane. The six `shfl.sync.idx` reads of the winner's state (group, begin, end, start, tile count, and the next scan base or SF start) still read lane 0, because `shfl.sync` uses only the low 5 bits of the lane operand. Outputs are therefore correct today, but `winning_lane` is outside `[0, 31]`, the range the CuTe DSL documents for a `shfl_sync` source lane. Any other use of the value (a compare, an index, a different clamp) would be wrong.

Reproducer on an RTX PRO 6000 (SM120): a CuTe DSL kernel in which warp `w` votes the suffix ballot `lane >= w`, then evaluates the template's expression next to the unsigned one and reads `lane_idx` back through `shfl.sync.idx`:

```
lowest winning lane  0: template winning_lane= 32 shfl src= 0 | unsigned winning_lane= 0 shfl src= 0
lowest winning lane  1: template winning_lane=  1 shfl src= 1 | unsigned winning_lane= 1 shfl src= 1
lowest winning lane 31: template winning_lane= 31 shfl src=31 | unsigned winning_lane=31 shfl src=31
```

In the templates themselves, for example the bf16 MoE grouped matmul with 34 groups (S = 421, N = K = 128, `CONFIG_sm120_128x128x128_16x16x32_cluster1x1_warps4x2`), the kernel PTX on develop has `bfind.s32 %r812, %r813;` followed by `sub.s32 ..., 31, %r812;`. The swap-AB template and both NVFP4 block-scale templates have the same instruction. Expected is `bfind.u32`.

`bfind.u32` of `brev(ballot)` is the position of the highest set bit, that is `31 - (lowest set lane)`, so the expression returns the lowest set lane for every non-zero ballot (0 for an all-lanes ballot). `32 - popc(ballot)` would also give the right lane, but only while the ballot is a suffix mask; the unsigned bit find does not depend on that. With a decreasing `first_token_offset` (invalid input) the ballot need not be a suffix mask. When lane 0 succeeds in such a ballot, the signed form picked the lowest failing lane (ballot `0x5`: lane 1), while the unsigned form picks the lowest succeeding lane (lane 0), which is the group the scan is looking for. When lane 0 fails, the two forms agree.

The linear-attention Frost code already writes this search on an unsigned word: `python/cudnn/linear_attention/frost/common/gdn2_state_grad.py:73-75` converts its ballot word to `Uint32` before `brev` / `bfind`.

Found in an audit of the SM120 Frost kernel templates (finding B36).

## Related issues

None.

Related PRs from the same audit (each of their branches merges with this one without conflicts, checked with `git merge-tree`):

- #2032 (finding B04, "clamp MoE group bounds to the routed rows") edits nearby lines of the same scheduler scan in the same four templates; the two changes do not overlap. Its clamp keeps every group at `0 <= begin <= end`, so no tile count can be negative and the ballot is a suffix mask for any offset table; the non-suffix case under Why then no longer arises.
- #2010 (B02), #2013 (B14), #2027 (B18) and #2028 (B21) edit other parts of these templates: the K-tail scale loads of the two block-scale templates (B02), the token-axis AVG epilogue (B14), a comment at the host-side scheduler-counter initialization (B18), and an assertion on the AB stage count in the two bf16 templates (B21).

## API and compatibility impact

None. The shuffles read the same lane as before, so outputs do not change, and the kernels' PTX differs only in the `bfind` instruction. No host-side or public API change.

The four SM100 MoE templates contain the same expression. They are intentionally left unchanged in this PR (the repository convention is that such a fix lands in both trees) for a follow-up:

- `python/cudnn/gemm/frost/sm100/kernel_templates/sm100_moe_grouped_matmul_fwd.py:474`
- `python/cudnn/gemm/frost/sm100/kernel_templates/sm100_moe_grouped_matmul_fwd_swap_ab.py:473`
- `python/cudnn/gemm/frost/sm100/kernel_templates/sm100_moe_grouped_block_scale_matmul_fwd.py:601`
- `python/cudnn/gemm/frost/sm100/kernel_templates/sm100_moe_grouped_block_scale_matmul_fwd_swap_ab.py:593`

FlashInfer's cuDNN Frost MoE backend ships standalone sources exported from the Frost MoE templates (`flashinfer/fused_moe/backends/cudnn_frost/artifacts/*/sources/`). At FlashInfer main b1cf76608, 85 of them carry the old expression: 28 `sm120_*` sources exported from the SM120 MoE templates, which pick up this fix only when they are re-exported, and 57 `sm107_*` sources exported from the SM100 templates above. Their outputs are unaffected for the same reason: every use of `winning_lane` in them is the lane operand of a `shfl.sync.idx` with clamp `0x1F`.

## Testing

GPU: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (SM120). CUDA 13.4, nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.7.1, torch 2.14.0+cu130, cuDNN 9.24, frontend bindings built from develop 24a8cd43. The runs marked 4.8.1 replace only the CuTe DSL with nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.8.1 (the release line of the `pyproject.toml` floor, `>=4.8.0`).

New tests (module-level L0, `requires_sm120`):

- `gemm/frost/test_moe_grouped_matmul_fwd.py::test_sm120_moe_scheduler_lane_search_is_unsigned[False|True]` (bf16, both orientations)
- `gemm/frost/test_moe_grouped_block_scale_matmul_fwd.py::test_sm120_moe_block_scale_scheduler_lane_search_is_unsigned[False|True]` (NVFP4, both orientations)

Each runs 34 groups (128 rows, 31 empty groups, then 256 and 37 rows; one expert per group), so lane 0 wins both for a claim in group 0 and for a claim in group 32, the first group of the second 32-group window. It compares the routed output with the torch reference, then requires the kernel PTX to contain the ballot and requires every `bfind` that reads a `brev.b32` result (the lane search; there must be at least one) to be `bfind.u32`. Other `bfind`s in the module, which also holds the scheduler-counter initialization kernel, are not checked.

```
cd test/python
python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider -p no:xdist gemm/frost/test_moe_grouped_matmul_fwd.py gemm/frost/test_moe_grouped_block_scale_matmul_fwd.py -k lane_search_is_unsigned
```

- develop 24a8cd43 with the new tests copied in: `4 failed, 1266 deselected, 4 warnings in 4.35s`. Every case fails at the lane-search assertion (`['bfind.s32']`), after the numerical comparison passed.
- this branch: `4 passed, 1266 deselected, 4 warnings in 4.11s`
- 4.8.1: develop `4 failed, 1266 deselected, 4 warnings in 16.06s` (the same assertion in every case), this branch `4 passed, 1266 deselected, 4 warnings in 3.92s`.

A CuTe DSL micro-kernel votes 4072 ballots through `nvvm.vote_sync` (the 32 suffix masks, 32 single lanes, 8 hand-picked masks such as `0x5` and `0x80000001`, and 4000 random words) and evaluates both expressions. With 4.7.1 and with 4.8.1 alike, the new expression gives the lowest set lane for every ballot. The develop expression gives 32 for the all-lanes ballot, the lowest failing lane for all 1987 ballots that contain lane 0 and are not all-lanes, and the same lane as the new expression for all 2084 ballots without lane 0. In both versions the ballot is an `Int32`, `brev` keeps its operand type, and the `Uint32` conversion emits no instruction (both `bfind`s read the same `brev.b32` result).

Related existing tests:

- `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider -p no:xdist gemm/frost -k sm120`
  - develop 24a8cd43: `1 failed, 1036 passed, 82 skipped, 9789 deselected, 201 warnings in 292.75s`
  - this branch: `1 failed, 1040 passed, 82 skipped, 9789 deselected, 4 warnings in 15.52s` (warm compile caches; a cold run of the first commit gave the same counts with 205 warnings in 295.66s)
  - The failure is `test_matmul.py::test_sm120_epi_vec_clamp_and_stg_only` on both (a dense-GEMM store-mode assertion, unrelated to this change); the four extra passes are the new tests.
- `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider -p no:xdist gemm/frost/test_template_epilogue_parity.py`: `42 passed, 2 skipped` on both.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: black, black-jupyter and the SPDX header check pass.

Not tested: SM10.x GPUs (the sm120 pipeline is also active there, but no such GPU was available, so the new tests are gated to SM120); CuTe DSL versions other than 4.7.1 and 4.8.1 (in both, `cute.arch.bfind` picks the instruction from the operand type: `Int32` gives `bfind.s32`, `Uint32` gives `bfind.u32`); the related existing tests under 4.8.1 (only the new tests and the micro-kernel ran with it). The SM100 templates are unchanged.

At FlashInfer main b1cf76608, 85 of them carry the old expression: 28 `sm120_*` sources exported from the SM120 MoE templates, which pick up this fix only when they are re-exported, and 57 `sm107_*` sources exported from the SM100 templates above. Their outputs are unaffected for the same reason: every use of `winning_lane` in them is the lane operand of a `shfl.sync.idx` with clamp `0x1F`.

## Testing

GPU: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (SM120). CUDA 13.4, nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.7.1, torch 2.14.0+cu130, cuDNN 9.24, frontend bindings built from develop 24a8cd43. Each runs 34 groups (128 rows, 31 empty groups, then 256 and 37 rows; one expert per group), so lane 0 wins both for a claim in group 0 and for a claim in group 32, the first group of the second 32-group window. It compares the routed output with the torch reference, then requires the kernel PTX to contain the ballot and requires every `bfind` that reads a `brev.b32` result (the lane search; there must be at least one) to be `bfind.u32`. A CuTe DSL micro-kernel votes 4072 ballots through `nvvm.vote_sync` (the 32 suffix masks, 32 single lanes, 8 hand-picked masks such as `0x5` and `0x80000001`, and 4000 random words) and evaluates both expressions. With 4.7.1 and with 4.8.1 alike, the new expression gives the lowest set lane for every ballot. +def keep_kernel_ptx(monkeypatch, compiler, dump_dir) -> None:
+    """Compile the kernels ``compiler`` (a family compiler module) renders in this test
+    with ``--keep-ptx`` and without the persistent compiled cache, whose reloaded object
+    carries no PTX; the PTX files and the generated sources (unique to ``dump_dir``) stay

+    monkeypatch.setenv("CUDNN_FRONTEND_DISABLE_COMPILED_CACHE", "1")

+    monkeypatch.setattr(compiler, "_FROST_COMPILE_OPTIONS", f"{compiler._FROST_COMPILE_OPTIONS} --keep-ptx --dump-dir={dump_dir}".strip())

+def kernel_ptx(compiled) -> str:
+    """The PTX of a plan (or :class:`Plan`) compiled under :func:`keep_kernel_ptx`."""
+    ptx = getattr(compiled, "_compiled", compiled)._launchable.__ptx__

+    result of the same function: each lowest-set-bit search ``31 - bfind(brev(x))``."""

+    for body in re.split(r"\.(?:entry|func)\s", ptx)[1:]:  # PTX registers are scoped to their function
